newsitem.title: CHINA: China auction in step toward bankruptcies.
newsitem.headline: China auction in step toward bankruptcies.

text.p: China took another small step toward forcing inefficient state companies into bankruptcy on Wednesday when it auctioned off the property of three failed concerns.
Several hundred hopeful buyers crowded into a Beijing auction hall to bid on the remnants of three companies, snapping up bargains from bricks and steel bars to mobile telephones and motorcycles.
"This was a good day. I saved at least 40 percent," said Wang Guoyi of Beijing Huawen Housing Company, obviously pleased with his purchases of a car and a mobile phone.
Another successful bidder was construction company official Wang Ming, who said he had travelled from the southeastern province of Fujian to buy building materials.

"I can't use all of the materials I bought but this was definitely a saving," he said after outbidding rivals in a heated contest, agreeing to pay 53,000 yuan ($6,400) for pipes and steel building materials.
"This was my first time at an auction," he said, though his bidding tactics seemed to suggest more than the skill of a novice.

China's lumbering state companies, saddled with debt and burdened with bloated workforces, have often been unable to compete in the sink-or-swim marketplace created after economic reforms began dismantling a centrally planned economy in 1979.
Officials have inched slowly toward pushing larger firms into bankruptcy, fearing that widespread layoffs would lead to social unrest.
The three bankrupt companies up for auction -- Fengtai Metal Products, Fengtai Wood Products and Fengtai Materials Trading -- had a combined workforce of only 100 people.

Liu Yu, an official with Beijing's Fengtai district committee on economic reform, said the employees of these companies would probably have to look for new jobs -- a huge shift away from the cradle-to-grave care provided under egalitarian leader Chairman Mao Zedong.
"The usual procedure is to get them to look for work elsewhere," he said.
The auction raised about 550,000 yuan for the companies that had total debts of some 26 million yuan, officials said.
While China has sold off other bankrupt companies before, this time it broke up the assets of the state-run firms and sold them piecemeal.
"This works for the type of goods we had for sale today," said Zhou Yun, auctioneer for the Beijing city government's auction company.
"These were products that ordinary individuals would be interested in," he said after he ended the auction, banging the gavel for the last time on Wednesday.
"I'm pleased with today's results," he said. "We sold off almost everything we had for sale."
